sources.procedure: scripts/segment_nextbrain.py: SuperSynth, then NextBrain Bayesian segmentation (segment_fireants.py --mode invivo --device cpu) of each hemisphere at 0.4 mm, joined on one 0.4 mm surface-RAS grid

crop.rule: bounding box of brain.mgz > 0, plus 20 voxels, within the grid

hemisphere_join.method: nearest neighbour from each hemisphere's own grid onto one surface-RAS grid
hemisphere_join.overlap_rule: sign of SuperSynth's MNI x coordinate at the voxel centre, the rule FreeSurfer splits hemispheres by

near_ties.rule: the runner-up label wherever NextBrain's winning posterior led it by less than the margin; 0 elsewhere and where the runner-up is background
near_ties.posteriors: written by scripts/freesurfer/run_patched.py from segment_fireants.py's label loop, beside a label update it leaves unchanged

runtime_workarounds.conv3d_slices: FreeSurfer 8.2's arm64 torch 2.1.2 has no oneDNN, so CPU conv3d builds a whole-volume im2col buffer (about 90 GB for SuperSynth). scripts/freesurfer/conv3d_slices.py computes the same stride-1 convolution as a sum over kernel depth of 2D convolutions of shifted slices: the same products in a different summation order, matching torch conv3d to 1e-5 relative. Only a convolution whose im2col buffer would reach 1 GiB is sliced; smaller ones run in torch itself, so NextBrain's bias field fit keeps the exact zeros it takes logs of. FireANTs keeps the builtin F.conv3d, which its TorchScript functions bind when they compile.
runtime_workarounds.supersynth_memory_releases: SuperSynth's inference.py drops its first-pass network outputs before the flipped pass, and the flipped outputs once they are averaged in. Only when memory is freed changes.
runtime_workarounds.opencv_stand_in: FreeSurfer 8.2's macOS Python has no OpenCV, yet ERC_bayesian_segmentation's ext/my_functions.py imports cv2 at module level for one helper that asserts False on entry. A stand-in module lets the import succeed and raises if any attribute of it is used.

sources.procedure: scripts/segment_spinal_cord.py: sct_deepseg spinalcord, sct_label_vertebrae -c t1, sct_register_to_template -c t1 with the disc labels, then sct_warp_template onto a 0.5 mm grid around the cord; each voxel takes its most probable PAM50 region where the region probabilities sum to at least 0.5, leaving out the unresolved regions [10, 11]
